market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: Historical patterns show that when a term-limited president leaves office, the opposing party wins 80% of the time (only exception 1988). With Trump term-limited after a second term, the Republican nominee will face this strong anti-incumbent headwind. Even accounting for unpredictable events, the true probability of a Republican win is likely around 30%, significantly below the market's 38.5%.
evidence_points: In the five open-seat elections following a term-limited president since WWII, the incumbent party held the White House only once (1988).
Without the sitting president on the ballot, the incumbent party loses the advantages of incumbency, making it harder to retain the presidency.
Long-range forecasts inherently have high uncertainty, but the historical baseline suggests a lower-than-market probability for the GOP.
